This vignette lowers intervention programs to `DiffEqCallbacks.jl` callbacks and
applies them to an SIR model implemented with `AlgebraicPetri.jl`. It uses the
same parameterization as the StockFlow and AlgebraicDynamics vignettes, following
[`epirecipes/sir-julia`](https://github.com/epirecipes/sir-julia): `S(0)=990`,
`I(0)=10`, `R(0)=0`, contact rate `c=10`, transmission probability `β=0.05`,
and recovery rate `γ=0.25`.

The key point is that AlgebraicPetri models naturally use labels for species and
transition rates. `PetriIndexing(parameters=[:inf, :rec], states=[:S, :I, :R])`
therefore uses the labels themselves as selectors, avoiding brittle positional
indexing.

```{julia}
using AlgebraicPetri
using CategoricalInterventions
using DiffEqCallbacks
using LabelledArrays
using OrdinaryDiffEq
using Plots

default(; linewidth=2, grid=false)

sir_model = LabelledPetriNet(
    [:S, :I, :R],
    :inf => ((:S, :I) => (:I, :I)),
    :rec => (:I => :R),
)

u0 = LVector(S=990.0, I=10.0, R=0.0)
p0 = LVector(inf=0.05 * 10.0 / sum(u0), rec=0.25)
tspan = (0.0, 40.0)

prob = ODEProblem(vectorfield(sir_model), u0, tspan, p0)
baseline = solve(prob, Tsit5(); saveat=0.5)

baseline.retcode, baseline[3, end], sum(baseline.u[end])
```

## A parameter intervention: lockdown

A lockdown is represented as a multiplicative reduction in the infection transition
rate `:inf` over an interval.

```{julia}
indexing = PetriIndexing(parameters=[:inf, :rec], states=[:S, :I, :R])

inf_rate = Target(
    :inf;
    kind=Parameter,
    value_type=Float64,
    algebra=MultiplicativeAlgebra(),
)

lockdown = InterventionProgram(
    InterventionAtom(:lockdown, inf_rate, Interval(5.0, 25.0), Scale(0.5)),
)

lockdown_cb = to_callback(lockdown, indexing; baseline_p=p0)
lockdown_sol = solve(prob, Tsit5(); callback=lockdown_cb, saveat=0.5)

lockdown_sol.retcode, lockdown_sol[3, end], sum(lockdown_sol.u[end])
```

The lower final recovered count indicates that the reduced infection rate prevented
some infections.

## A state intervention: vaccination

Vaccination is a state transfer rather than a parameter change. It can be encoded as
two simultaneous state pulses: remove people from `:S` and add them to `:R`.

```{julia}
susceptible = Target(:S; kind=State, value_type=Float64, algebra=AdditiveAlgebra())
recovered = Target(:R; kind=State, value_type=Float64, algebra=AdditiveAlgebra())

vaccination = InterventionProgram(
    InterventionAtom(:vaccinate_from_s, susceptible, Interval(15.0, 16.0), Add(-50.0)),
    InterventionAtom(:vaccinate_to_r, recovered, Interval(15.0, 16.0), Add(50.0)),
)

vaccination_cb = to_callback(vaccination, indexing)
vaccination_sol = solve(prob, Tsit5(); callback=vaccination_cb, saveat=0.5)

vaccination_sol.retcode, vaccination_sol[1, end], sum(vaccination_sol.u[end])
```

The vaccination callback preserves total population because the state intervention
is encoded as a transfer.

## Composing lockdown and vaccination

The parameter intervention and the state transfer target different components, so
they compose without conflict.

```{julia}
combined = compose_interventions(lockdown, vaccination)
combined_cb = to_callback(combined, indexing; baseline_p=p0)
combined_sol = solve(prob, Tsit5(); callback=combined_cb, saveat=0.5)

(
    baseline_R = baseline[3, end],
    lockdown_R = lockdown_sol[3, end],
    vaccination_S = vaccination_sol[1, end],
    combined_R = combined_sol[3, end],
    combined_total = sum(combined_sol.u[end]),
)
```

The same intervention program can be inspected before it is lowered to callbacks.

```{julia}
[(epoch.support, collect(keys(epoch.effects))) for epoch in epochize(combined)]
```

## Cross-check against the same SIR equations

The same intervention program should give the same trajectory when applied to
the direct SIR equations. This guards against accidentally changing the meaning
of `:inf`, `:rec`, `:S`, `:I`, or `:R` across representations.

```{julia}
function sir_ode(u, p, t)
    infection = p.inf * u.S * u.I
    recovery = p.rec * u.I
    return LVector(S=-infection, I=infection - recovery, R=recovery)
end

reference_prob = ODEProblem(sir_ode, u0, tspan, p0)

reference_baseline = solve(reference_prob, Tsit5(); saveat=0.5)
reference_combined = solve(
    reference_prob,
    Tsit5();
    callback=to_callback(combined, indexing; baseline_p=p0),
    saveat=0.5,
)

max_reference_difference = maximum(abs, Array(baseline) .- Array(reference_baseline))
max_combined_difference = maximum(abs, Array(combined_sol) .- Array(reference_combined))

max_reference_difference, max_combined_difference
```

```{julia}
max_reference_difference < 1e-6 && max_combined_difference < 1e-6
```

## Plotting the intervention scenarios

The final recovered counts summarize the epidemic size, but plotting the whole
trajectory shows when each intervention has its main effect.

```{julia}
plot(
    baseline.t,
    baseline[3, :];
    label="baseline",
    xlabel="time",
    ylabel="R(t)",
    title="Recovered population under intervention scenarios",
)
plot!(lockdown_sol.t, lockdown_sol[3, :]; label="lockdown")
plot!(vaccination_sol.t, vaccination_sol[3, :]; label="vaccination")
plot!(combined_sol.t, combined_sol[3, :]; label="combined")
```

The combined scenario can also be inspected by compartment.

```{julia}
plot(
    combined_sol.t,
    combined_sol[1, :];
    label="S",
    xlabel="time",
    ylabel="population",
    title="Combined lockdown and vaccination scenario",
)
plot!(combined_sol.t, combined_sol[2, :]; label="I")
plot!(combined_sol.t, combined_sol[3, :]; label="R")
```
